name: Shethar-bozenai
overview: Shethar-bozenai is a male figure noted in the book of Ezra as one who opposed the rebuilding of the Temple in Jerusalem. His actions are specifically recorded in Ezra 5:3, highlighting his role in resisting the restoration efforts of Israel. No additional tribal affiliation or personal notes are provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The only recorded name for this individual is Shethar-bozenai, with no given meaning or divine origin noted. The name appears in Ezra 5:3 and serves simply as a proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Shethar-bozenai beyond what is mentioned in his opposition to the Temple rebuilding. There are no known relatives or connections listed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shethar-bozenai's significance lies in his opposition to the rebuilding of the Temple, a critical project for the restoration of Israel's worship and covenant relationship with God. His resistance represents the external challenges faced by the returned exiles in fulfilling God's purposes. This opposition underscores the spiritual and political obstacles encountered during the post-exilic period.
